overall_summary: Bitcoin faces a mixed session with strong spot ETF inflows providing support, while Strategy selling, security bugs, and a major bank cutting exposure weigh on sentiment. Soft labor data and easing yields lean dovish for risk assets, but elevated geopolitical tensions from the Middle East to Ukraine and US-China frictions keep markets cautious ahead of key jobs data.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs see $626M three-day inflows
Strategy dumps another $105M BTC; Italy bank cuts ETF
Soft ADP payrolls and easing yields trim hike bets
Geopolitical risks rise: Houthis, Russia, China curbs
Focus turns to jobless claims and Friday NFP

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Pull In $626M Over Three Days
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded two hundred forty-four million dollars in net inflows on August fifth alone, bringing the three-day total to roughly six hundred twenty-six million. That is the strongest pace since early May and comes as Bitcoin hovers near sixty-four to sixty-five thousand. Traders should care because sustained ETF buying has been the primary institutional bid absorbing supply this year. If the streak holds, it could finally break Bitcoin out of its multi-week range.
items.impact: Supports price via renewed institutional demand

items.title: Lummis Pushes Senate CLARITY Act Vote Before Recess
items.summary: Senator Cynthia Lummis says she believes the Senate will vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before the August recess and may even work through the weekend. The bill would clarify commodity versus security status and set rules for exchanges and custody. Traders should watch this closely because passage would lift a major regulatory overhang that has capped institutional flows. A delay or failure would likely keep Bitcoin range-bound into the fall.
items.impact: Major unresolved catalyst; passage bullish, delay extends uncertainty

items.title: Coldcard Wallet Flaw Drains Over $100M in Bitcoin
items.summary: A long-dormant firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets has enabled hackers to steal more than one hundred million dollars in Bitcoin across multiple waves by predicting seed phrases. Thousands of addresses were drained without physical access to the devices. Analysts note the episode damages self-custody confidence but could accelerate demand for regulated ETFs and professional custodians. Traders should monitor for further waves and any rotation into spot products.
items.impact: Short-term sentiment hit; potential boost to ETF and custody demand

items.title: Strategy Sells Another $105 Million of Bitcoin
items.summary: Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, sold one thousand six hundred thirty-eight BTC last week for about one hundred five million dollars at an average near sixty-four thousand. Proceeds funded preferred dividends and STRC share repurchases while the firm builds a multi-billion cash reserve. This continues the shift from a pure hold-forever stance. Markets care because sales by the biggest public holder, even in modest size, can pressure sentiment and signal ongoing supply.
items.impact: Negative sentiment and incremental selling pressure from largest holder

items.title: Bitcoin Devs Flag 85 Critical Bugs in AI Audit
items.summary: A volunteer team of sixteen developers ran AI models against nearly four hundred Bitcoin-related projects and uncovered eighty-five critical bugs plus hundreds of high-severity issues in little more than a day. They describe the situation as extremely bad and are rushing reports to maintainers. The effort lands right after the Coldcard exploit and shows AI accelerating both offense and defense. Traders should note the elevated risk of further exploits that could shake confidence across wallets and infrastructure.
items.impact: Raises ecosystem security risks and potential for more hacks

items.title: Italy's Largest Bank Slashes Bitcoin ETF by 94%
items.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo cut its BlackRock IBIT holdings by roughly ninety-four percent in the second quarter while tripling its stake in a staked Ethereum ETF that pays yield. The bank retained other Bitcoin exposure but clearly rotated toward yield-bearing products. The Form thirteen F filing highlights selective institutional preference for Ethereum staking returns that spot Bitcoin funds cannot match. It is a signal that capital can shift inside crypto even without broad risk-off moves.
items.impact: Highlights institutional rotation from BTC ETFs toward yield assets

items.title: Fed's Cook Ready to Hike Rates if Inflation Stays High
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said she is prepared to raise interest rates if inflation does not start easing soon. She called inflation too high at 3.7 percent on the PCE measure and noted risks are skewed toward prices rather than jobs. The economy remains resilient with solid growth and a stable low-hire low-fire labor market. Traders should care because this keeps the door open for a September hike after the divided July hold, potentially pressuring risk assets including Bitcoin if data stays sticky.
items.impact: Raises odds of tighter policy, weighing on risk assets

items.title: ADP Private Payrolls Rise Just 44,000 in July
items.summary: Private employers added only 44,000 jobs in July according to ADP, well below the roughly 70,000 expected and the weakest reading in six months after a revised 95,000 in June. Pay growth held firm year-over-year. This soft labor signal comes right before Friday's official jobs report. Crypto traders should watch it because weaker hiring reduces near-term pressure for Fed hikes and has already helped ease bond yields.
items.impact: Softens rate-hike bets, supportive for risk assets short-term

items.title: July Challenger Job Cuts Fall to Two-Year Low
items.summary: US employers announced just 33,429 job cuts in July, the lowest monthly total in two years and down sharply from June's 45,849. Tech still led the reductions with AI as a key theme, but overall hiring plans rose to the strongest July since 2022. This points to a still-resilient labor market with low layoffs. For traders it reinforces the low-fire environment the Fed is watching and may limit downside risks ahead of the official payrolls number.
items.impact: Supports labor resilience narrative, mixed for rate path

items.title: Treasury Yields Ease as Markets Pare Fed Hike Bets
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 4.63 percent on Thursday after dropping about 10 basis points this week. Softer ADP data plus hopes for a Hormuz shipping corridor that could lower oil prices have cooled inflation fears and cut expected Fed hikes this year to roughly one. The dollar index sits around 99.8. Bitcoin traders care because lower yields and reduced tightening odds usually ease financial conditions and support risk appetite.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions positive for crypto and equities

items.title: Markets Eye Today's Productivity and Jobless Claims
items.summary: Thursday brings the preliminary Q2 nonfarm productivity and unit labor costs report plus weekly initial jobless claims. Consensus looks for productivity around plus 0.6 percent after a weak 0.3 percent prior quarter and claims near 200,000. These prints feed directly into the inflation and labor picture the Fed is tracking. Crypto traders should stay alert because a soft claims number or strong productivity could reinforce the case against immediate hikes while the opposite would firm the dollar and yields.
items.impact: Data-dependent catalyst ahead of Friday NFP

items.title: Focus Shifts to Friday NFP After Soft Labor Signals
items.summary: All eyes turn to Friday's July employment report after the weak ADP print and low Challenger cuts. Economists expect modest job gains around the prior 57,000 pace with unemployment near 4.2 percent. The Fed remains divided after its July hold at 3.5 to 3.75 percent with three hike dissents. This is the key near-term macro event for rates pricing. Traders need to position carefully because a hot number could revive September hike odds while a miss would fuel risk-on moves in Bitcoin.
items.impact: High-volatility event that can swing rate expectations

items.title: Iran, Oman Near Hormuz Deal; Trump Eyes Quick Reopening
items.summary: Iran and Oman say they are in the final stages of an agreement on managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint announcement expected soon. President Trump has said a deal could come this week and expressed preference for diplomacy over more strikes, though sources indicate the proposal may give Iran significant control over inbound traffic and potential fees. Oil prices have already dropped sharply on the hopes of restored flows through the key chokepoint that normally handles a large share of global oil. Traders should watch closely because a genuine reopening would ease energy prices and inflation pressures, supporting risk assets including crypto, while failure or Iranian hardline conditions could reverse the relief rally fast.
items.impact: Potential sharp drop in oil and risk-on move if deal seals

items.title: Houthis Claim Missile Strike on Saudi Oil Tanker
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they launched a ballistic missile attack on a Saudi oil tanker off the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The claim comes amid ongoing threats to Saudi shipping and reports of reduced Gulf traffic. No immediate Saudi confirmation was available, but the attack adds another layer of risk to energy routes already strained by the Hormuz situation. Crypto traders care because further Red Sea or Gulf disruptions keep a geopolitical premium in oil prices, which can weigh on risk sentiment and complicate the de-escalation narrative from Hormuz talks.
items.impact: Sustains oil supply fears and risk-off pressure

items.title: US Depletes Virtually All Long-Range Precision Missiles
items.summary: The US Army has used up virtually all of its stockpile of ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles during the five-month war with Iran, according to sources familiar with the data. This raises serious questions about readiness for other contingencies and may limit options for further major strikes. Reports also note heavy use of air-defense interceptors. For markets this signals potential constraints on US military posture, which could embolden adversaries or force a faster diplomatic off-ramp, keeping geopolitical uncertainty elevated for risk assets.
items.impact: Highlights US munitions strain and strategic limits

items.title: North Korea Deploys Missile Unit to Russia for Ukraine
items.summary: A North Korean ballistic missile unit of around 90 personnel has begun deploying to Russia's Voronezh region and could bring up to 120 missiles and six launchers for use against Ukraine, according to Ukrainian military intelligence. This expands already deep military cooperation and comes as Ukraine struggles with depleted high-end air defenses. Russia has already used North Korean missiles in recent strikes. The move escalates the Ukraine conflict, increases ballistic missile threats that Patriots struggle to counter, and adds another layer of great-power tension that typically pressures risk assets.
items.impact: Deepens Ukraine war escalation and air-defense strain

items.title: Russia Ballistic Strike Kills 17 Around Kyiv
items.summary: Russian forces launched a major overnight ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv and surrounding areas, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. Ukraine reported it intercepted none of the roughly two dozen ballistic and hypersonic missiles, underscoring critically low interceptor stocks. The strike targeted civilian and logistics sites. Continued high-intensity attacks and Ukraine's air-defense shortages keep the war hot and raise the odds of further Western involvement or energy market spillover via Black Sea routes, weighing on broader risk appetite.
items.impact: Sustains Ukraine war intensity and interceptor crisis

items.title: China Hits US with Drone Export Curbs and Sanctions
items.summary: China announced countermeasures including strict case-by-case controls on drone and dual-use technology exports to the United States, plus a ban on dealings with several American entities. The moves respond to recent US restrictions on Chinese drones and forced-labor related lists. Given China's dominance in commercial drones and components, this tightens supply chains and escalates the tech and trade confrontation. For traders it adds another headwind to global growth and tech-related risk assets at a time when multiple geopolitical fronts are already active.
items.impact: Escalates US-China tech/trade frictions and supply risks
